title: I Looked at the Corpse
text:
I looked at the corpse, his swift visible order
+and the slowest disorder of his soul;
+I saw him survive; within his mouth
+the broken-off age of two mouths.
+They shouted his number to him: pieces.
+They shouted his love to him: better had he not!
+They shouted his bullet to him: dead as well!
+
+And his digestive order held
+while his soul’s disorder, behind, held on in vain.
+They left him and heard him, and it is then
+that the corpse
+almost lived in secret, for an instant;
+but they listened to him mentally—and dates!
+wept into his ear—and dates as well!
editorial_note: The body’s clinical order is set against the soul’s radically slowed disorder; the repeated dates remain unexplained verdicts rather than being normalized into chronology.

title: Trilce: Poem XLIV — This Piano Travels Inward
text:
This piano travels inward,
+travels in joyous leaps.
+Then meditates in iron-shod repose,
+nailed down by ten horizons.
+
+It advances. Drags itself beneath tunnels,
+farther on, beneath tunnels of pain,
+beneath vertebrae naturally in flight.
+
+At other times its trunks go by,
+slow yellow Asias of living,
+go by eclipse,
+and delouse themselves of insectile nightmares,
+already dead to thunder, herald of the geneses.
+
+Dark piano, whom do you spy
+with your deafness that hears me,
+with your ripeness that deafens me?
+
+O mysterious pulse.
editorial_note: The source’s anomalous asias is retained as Asias, allowing both bodily yearning and continental reach to haunt the piano; ferrado stays materially iron-shod.

title: Trilce: Poem LIV — Outlaw Torment, Enter, Leave
text:
Outlaw torment, enter, leave
+through one same quadrangular hole.
+Doubt. The balance stabs and stabs
+up to the hilt.
+
+At times I strike against all counterstrikes,
+and for a while I am the blackest high of the apices
+in Harmony’s fatality.
+Then the dark circles under the eyes flare divinely,
+and the saw of the soul sobs,
+oxygens of goodwill turn violent,
+all that does not burn burns, and even
+pain crooks its beak into laughter.
+
+But one day you will not be able to enter
+or leave, with the fistful of earth
+I shall throw into your eyes, outlaw!
editorial_note: The repeated contras become counterstrikes, carrying opposition and collision; sierra remains a saw so its sob can cut through the physiological and musical field.

title: Trilce: Poem XLV — I Sever My Ties with the Sea
text:
I sever my ties with the sea
+when the waters come to me.
+
+Let us always go out. Let us savor
+the stupendous song, the song uttered
+by desire’s lower lips.
+O prodigious maidenhood.
+The saltless breeze passes.
+
+Far off I scent the marrow
+hearing the deep groping, hunting
+for undertow keys.
+
+And if in this way we came nose-first
+against the absurd,
+we would cover ourselves with the gold of having nothing,
+and brood the still-unborn wing
+of night, sister
+to this orphaned wing of day,
+which by dint of being one is wing no longer.
editorial_note: Lower lips retain the erotic anatomy behind the song, while teclas keeps the poem’s submerged keyboard; the final single wing loses winghood through its very singularity.

title: Ostrich
text:
Melancholy, draw out your sweet beak now;
+
+do not fatten your fasts on my wheatfields of light.
+
+Melancholy, enough! How your daggers drink
+
+the blood my blue leech would draw!
+
+
+Do not finish the manna of woman that has descended;
+
+I want some cross to be born of it tomorrow,
+
+tomorrow, when I have no one toward whom to turn my eyes,
+
+when the coffin opens its great mocking O.
+
+
+My heart is a flowerpot watered with bitterness;
+
+other old birds graze inside it…
+
+Melancholy, stop drying the life from me,
+
+and strip bare your woman’s lip…!
editorial_note: The ostrich is never named within the address but survives in melancholy’s beak and devouring fast; the coffin’s O retains its visual and vocal mockery.

title: Trilce: Poem LXXIII — Another Ay Has Triumphed
text:
Another ay has triumphed. Truth is there.
+And whoever acts thus, will he not know
+how to train excellent digitigrades
+for the mouse Yes … No … ?
+
+Another ay has triumphed, and against no one.
+O exosmosis of chemically pure water.
+Ah my southerlies. O our divine ones.
+                                    I therefore have the right
+to be green and happy and dangerous, and to be
+the chisel, fear of the rough and vast block;
+to put my foot in it and into laughter.
+
+Absurd, you alone are pure.
+Absurd, only before you is this excess
+sweated out in golden pleasure.
editorial_note: Ay is left untranslated as cry, letter, and victorious entity; dijitígrados becomes digitigrades without repairing the bizarre training of creatures for the yes-no mouse.

title: Trilce: Poem LI — A Lie. I Did It Just to Deceive
text:
A lie. I did it just to deceive,
+and nothing more. That’s that. Otherwise,
+you too will see
+how much it will hurt me to have been this way.
+
+A lie. Be quiet.
+That’s enough.
+Since other times you do this same thing to me,
+that is why I too have been this way.
+
+Me, who had watched so very closely to see whether
+you truly cried,
+since other times you merely remained
+in your sweet little pouts;
+me, who never dreamed you would believe them—
+your tears got the better of me.
+That’s that.
+
+But now you know: it was all a lie.
+And if you keep on crying, well then!
+Next time I will not even look when you play.
editorial_note: The childlike quarrel is kept plain and breathlessly defensive; pucheros remains little pouts, holding together the face, staged tears, and diminutive tenderness.

title: Time, Time
text:
Noon stalled among damp chills.
+        The bored barracks pump bails out
+        time time time time.
+
+
+        Was Was.
+
+
+        Roosters song while scratching in vain.
+        Mouth of clear day conjugating
+        was was was was.
+
+
+        Tomorrow Tomorrow.
+
+
+        Rest still warm from being.
+        The present thinks keep me for
+        tomorrow tomorrow tomorrow tomorrow.
+
+
+        Name Name.
+
+
+        What is the name of all that bristles us?
+        Its name is Thesame that suffers
+        name name name name.
editorial_note: This distinct witness of Trilce II omits the opening Tiempo Tiempo and alters the final capitalization; the reviewed verbal mutations and its source-specific typography are preserved.
